discovery_plan.macro_recon_summary:
【宏观侦察综合综述 (Macro Reconnaissance Synthesis)】
基于2025-2026年全球与中国工业前沿证据库（EvidenceVault）的情报聚类，电力能源（power_energy）与半导体芯片制造（semiconductor）两大硬科技赛道正经历底层物理范式与工程边界的深刻重构，催生出前所未有的工业量检测（Industrial Metrology & Inspection）技术革命：

1. 电力能源领域（power_energy）：
驱动力由传统的“宏观离线安全抽检”全面转向“算力-能源协同高密热电安全、固态界面物理与全生命周期双碳计量”。一方面，AI智算大模型爆发导致全球智算中心能耗预计于2026年突破1,050 TWh，机柜功率密度攀升倒逼配电系统向800V高压直流（HVDC）微电网与直接液冷换热全面迁移，热-电耦合安全与微通道泄漏检测成为跨界刚需（[EV-CN-001], [EV-GLOBAL-001], [EV-GLOBAL-003], [EV-GLOBAL-005]）；另一方面，新型电力系统全面迈入314Ah+大容量储能电芯时代（中国电建16GWh大规模集采招标）与GWh级全固态电池、GW级钙钛矿叠层产线落地关键节点，固-固界面接触应力与光伏结晶相变缺陷成为制约良率核心卡点（[EV-CN-002], [EV-CN-006], [EV-CN-009]）；同时，中国绿氢产能占据全球74%及特高压环保绝缘气体替代SF6、火电调峰CCUS规模化，直接拉动高精度气体红外吸收光谱与声学相控阵在线监控需求（[EV-CN-011], [EV-CN-014], [EV-GLOBAL-007]）。

2. 半导体芯片制造领域（semiconductor）：
摩尔定律微缩受阻与算力互连带宽瓶颈共同推动半导体量检测迈向“跨尺度三维多物理场表征与光电协同”。中国大陆前道与先进封装量检测设备市场迎来高速扩张（2026年达数十亿美元，复合增速超17%，[EV-CN-036]）。在先进制程向GAA/3D NAND迈进的同时，无凸点Cu-Cu混合键合（Hybrid Bonding）与面板级/玻璃基板先进封装对纳米级凹陷（Dishing）与全场热翘曲（Warpage）提出了极高精度的白光干涉与超声成像要求（[EV-CN-026], [EV-GLOBAL-025], [EV-GLOBAL-026]）；CPO（共封装光学）与硅光芯片的崛起，颠覆了传统纯电学测试体系，创造了晶圆级高精度光纤亚微米对准与光-电-热原位协同测试的新蓝海（[EV-GLOBAL-039]）；而在AI高压电源与新能源汽车拉动下，8英寸SiC/GaN功率半导体外延晶格缺陷与晶圆级超高压动态KGD（Known Good Die）测试装备成为高端良率管控的核心命门（[EV-GLOBAL-002], [EV-GLOBAL-039]）。
discovery_plan.step_back_thesis:
【第一性原理退步物理假说 (Step-Back First-Principles Physics Thesis)】
工业量检测的本质并非外在几何尺寸的被动比对，而是在原子与微米介观尺度上，通过可控能量探针（光子、电子、声波、电磁波与热流）与物质界面的非平衡态能量及载流子输运过程发生相互作用，并对所激发的散射波场、相位延迟、辐射复合并发射能谱进行高信噪比反演。

其物理极限与测量瓶颈由三大第一性原理支配：
1. 波动力学分辨率与衍射极限（Wave Diffraction & Coherence Limits）：光学衍射极限遵循阿贝极限（$d \ge \frac{\lambda}{2 \cdot \text{NA}}$），在深亚微米及三维埋层结构中，常规明场成像失效，必须退步至波动相位反演——利用低相干干涉的纵向相干长度测量纳米级高度差，利用严格耦合波分析（RCWA）麦克斯韦电磁场空间谐波解析深纳米光栅关键尺寸（OCD），利用声阻抗失配系数（$R = \frac{Z_2 - Z_1}{Z_2 + Z_1}$）实现埋层纳米空洞的声场高对比度反射；
2. 非平衡载流子复合与量子受激发射（Non-Equilibrium Carrier Transport & Recombination）：在半导体与光伏活性层中，晶格缺陷（如位错、悬挂键、微管）本质上是禁带中的非辐射复合中心。外场激发的荧光强度与准费米能级分裂量直接相关（$I \propto \exp(\frac{E_F^n - E_F^p}{kT})$），通过全晶圆微区微秒级荧光寿命（PL）与受激辐射谱成像，能够无损直接探测出肉眼不可见的深能级晶格缺陷态；
3. 动态热-电多场耦合耗散动力学（Coupled Electro-Thermal-Fluidic Dissipation Dynamics）：高密电能传输与微流道冷却遵循麦克斯韦电磁发热定律（$Q = I^2 R_c$）与纳维-斯托克斯对流传热方程。接触界面的微观粗糙度收缩阻抗及交变热应力下的微孔气蚀，直接决定了宏观绝缘与换热失效。通过瞬态热阻谱（$Z_{th}$）与谐振微扰计量，能够在线预警灾难性击穿。

因此，工业量检测的战略重心正在从“离线静态形貌表征”根本性演进为“在线三维埋层多物理场输运断层扫描”。

records.title: 在液冷数据中心中，manifold液冷歧管（分水器/分流器）构成了冷却系统的核心分配网络
records.snippet:
01 歧管为何必须氦检：从“微漏”到“大患”的逻辑
manifold液冷歧管的密封可靠性是液冷系统的生命线。
其泄漏风险主要来源于：
数十至数百个焊接点，每个焊点都是潜在的微观缺陷区。
各种螺纹、法兰与快速接头，依赖密封圈的长期稳定性。
材料本身的微观孔隙或加工应力裂纹。
传统的水检或压降测试，只能发现较大的泄漏。
而液冷系统，尤其是使用介电流体的浸没式液冷，对微泄漏（低于10⁻⁵ mbar·L/s）极为敏感。
微泄漏会导致：
冷却液缓慢流失，系统压力与流量失衡，散热效率逐年下降。
空气或水分侵入，可能引发内部腐蚀或产生气泡，影响冷却均一性。
在风冷板式系统中，泄漏的冷却液可能直接导致电气设备短路故障。
因此，氦质谱检漏以其10⁻¹² mbar·L/s级的超高灵敏度，成为歧管制造与集成环节不可替代的终极检测手段，能在问题发生前实现“归零”预防。

records.title: 液冷进入‘零泄漏时代’：二次侧组件为何全面导入氦检？
records.snippet:
微通道冷板（MCCP）是未来趋势。
它将内部流道微缩至80–90μm，大幅增加换热面积，散热能力显著提升。
在英伟达规划的全液冷系统VR NVL 144中，运算层将采用MCCP水冷板直贴Vera Rubin芯片，使其成为遍布“精密液体血管”的高密度散热核心。
为何冷板必须做氦检？
1微泄漏检测能力
冷板内部流道复杂，多采用微通道真空钎焊。
氦分子极小，氦检可检出低至 10⁻¹² mbar·L/s的极微小漏点，远超水检、气泡检等传统方法，能在出厂前彻底排除隐患。
2保障设备与业务安全
数据中心液冷液多为导电或不导电冷却液。

records.title: 高压母线在线测试温度
records.snippet: 高压母线在线测试温度是电力系统中重要的监测课题。高压开关、GIS等设备在负载电流过大时易出现温升，可能导致绝缘性能劣化甚至击穿。因此，需有效监测母线及电接触温度。目前，温度测量主要采用涂色材料或红外测温仪，但准确度低、不便或成本高。为解决这些问题，采用数字温度传感器，通过热敏电阻测量温度，将阻值变化转换为脉冲信号，经处理后得到温度值。该传感器抗干扰能力强，精度高，适用于高压环境。传感器由CMOSIC构成，采用“减计数”方法减小测量误差，确保高温情况下的测量准确性。该方案能实现母线温度的实时在线监测，为电力系统状态综合监测提供支持。

2. 中游电源设备呈现多技术路线并行格局
中游环节是800V HVDC技术创新的集中区域，主要包含以下三种技术路径：
- 高压直流电源（HVDC）：技术成熟度较高，采用模块化冗余设计，满载效率在96%至98%之间，是目前应用最为广泛的方案。
代表企业包括中恒电气、科华数据和台达。-
直流UPS：体积更紧凑，效率较传统HVDC方案高出2至3个百分点，预制化程度高，适用于中小型AI数据中心。
易事特、科士达等企业在此领域具有一定优势。-
固态变压器（SST）：采用半导体器件替代传统铜绕组，体积和重量减少50%以上，效率超过98%，代表“硅进铜退”的技术方向。
目前该方案仍处于验证阶段，ABB、西门子、科华数据等企业正积极推进相关研发。

records.title: Constriction and contact impedance of ceramic solid electrolytes
records.snippet: 陶瓷固态电解质的收缩和接触阻抗。固态电池的发展受到循环过程中固-固界面退化的影响，可能导致空洞形成和接触损失。本文系统研究了电极/Li6PS5Cl界面的不可恢复和实际接触面积对阻抗谱的影响。通过调节施加的堆叠压力和控制接触几何形状，识别了它们在阻抗谱中的不同特征，并量化了它们对固态电解质界面电阻和有效离子电导率的影响。实验结果表明，更高的压力和改善的接触面积显著降低了界面电阻。界面电阻与压力呈幂律关系，指数为-0.5，提供了实际接触面积变化的见解。此外，分散接触比集中接触导致更低的阻抗，因为潜在梯度更小且电势分布更均匀。我们的模拟预测了接触几何形状的界面电阻，与实验结果一致。我们的工作强调了不可恢复和可恢复接触损失在控制固态电池阻抗中的不同作用。固态电池（SSBs）因其更高的安全性、能量密度和对热失控问题的缓解而被视为下一代储能技术。然而，固-固界面相比固-液界面带来了独特的挑战，阻碍了广泛应用。界面现象如空洞形成、应力诱导变形和接触损失导致界面电阻增加，阻碍离子传输。外部压力可以控制界面，但通常受限于几MPa，由于不可恢复空洞可能导致显著接触损失。解决这些挑战对提高SSB的性能、寿命和可靠性至关重要。电化学阻抗谱（EIS）是一种强大的非破坏性技术，用于探测SSB的界面接触。通过分析频率依赖的响应，EIS能够分离不同的阻抗贡献，如体传输、晶界效应和界面过程。这使得它特别适用于监测固-固界面在操作中的接触变化。Fleig和Maier发现，非理想接触在低频下有显著的收缩效应，但在高频下消失。EIS中也发现了界面粗糙度的特征。最近，Eckhardt等人表明，传统的1D等效电路模型不足以模拟SSB中接触引起的动态收缩。由于界面几何和电化学效应的相互作用，解释实验EIS数据具有挑战性。收缩或接触电阻难以从EIS数据中与其他现象的特征中分离。本文结合EIS实验和模拟，研究了电极/Li6PS5Cl固态电解质（SE）界面的接触形态对阻抗的影响，通过系统控制实验中的可恢复和不可恢复接触损失。不可恢复接触损失通过在界面区域阻断接触来精确控制。我们发现界面接触在EIS中的显著特征，通过界面电阻量化。我们绘制了界面电阻对不可恢复接触损失和由压力控制的可恢复接触损失的依赖关系。通过在宽压力范围内测量，我们发现界面电阻通常遵循与电
records.full_markdown:
Constriction and contact impedance of ceramic solid electrolytes
Abstract
The development of solid-state batteries is hindered by the degradation of the solid-solid interface during cycling which can cause void formation and contact loss. Here, we systematically investigate the effect of unrecoverable and real interfacial contact area at the electrode/\ceLi6PS5Cl interface on the impedance spectrum. By varying applied stack pressures and controlling contact geometries, we identify their distinct signatures in the impedance spectrum and quantify their influence on the interfacial resistance and effective ionic conductivity of the solid electrolyte. Experimental results demonstrate that higher pressures and improved contact areas significantly reduce interfacial resistance. The interfacial resistance scales with pressure according to power law with exponent of -0.5, providing insights into the variation of real contact area. Further, distributed contacts lead to lower impedance compared to concentrated contacts due to smaller potential gradients and a more uniform potential distribution. Our simulations predict interfacial resistances of the contact geometries in agreement with experiments. Our work emphasizes the distinct roles of unrecoverable and recoverable contact losses in controlling the impedance of solid-state batteries.
Solid-state batteries (SSBs) are considered a promising next-generation energy storage technology due to their potential for improved safety, higher energy density, and the mitigation of issues such as thermal runaway.1, 2, 3, 4, 5 However, solid-solid interfaces present unique challenges compared to solid-liquid interfaces that impede widespread adoption.6 Interfacial phenomena such as void formation, stress-induced deformation, and contact loss lead to increased interfacial resistance and hinder ionic transport.7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 While external pressure can offer control over the interface, it is often limited due to practical considerations to a few MPa where considerable contact loss may be present due to unrecoverable voids 13, 14, 15. Addressing these challenges is crucial for improving the performance, longevity, and reliability of SSBs.
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) offers a powerful non-destructive technique tool to probe interfacial contact in SSBs.16 By analyzing frequency-dependent responses, EIS enables the separation of different impedance contributions, such as bulk transport, grain boundary effects, and interfacial processes. This capability makes it especially useful for monitoring changes in contact at the solid-solid interfaces during operation. The differences in EIS at high and low frequencies due to non-ideal contacts were elucidated by Fleig and Maier17, 18 who found that constriction effects are significant at low frequencies but disappear at high frequencies. Signatures of interfacial roughness have also been found in the EIS 19, 20, 21. Recently, Eckhardt et al.22, 23 showed that conventional 1D equivalent circuit models are inadequate for modeling the dynamic constriction caused by contact in SSBs. Interpreting experimental EIS data can be challenging due to the interplay of geometric and electrochemical effects at the interface. Constriction or contact resistance has been difficult to isolate from signatures of other phenomena in EIS data 10 since interfacial contact cannot be directly controlled in experiments.
In this work, we combine EIS experiments and simulations to investigate the effect of contact morphology at the electrode/\ceLi6PS5Cl solid electrolyte (SE) interface on the impedance by systematically controlling the recoverable and unrecoverable contact loss in experiments. The unrecoverable contact loss is precisely controlled by blocking contact in regions of the interface. We find distinct signatures of interfacial contact in EIS quantified through the interfacial resistance. We map out the dependence of the interfacial resistance on both the unrecoverable contact loss and recoverable contact loss controlled by pressure. Through measurements over a wide pressure range, we find that the interfacial resistance generally scales as in agreement with electrical contact resistance theories.24. Further, the interfacial resistance rises rapidly as the unrecoverable contact area increases and can be approximated by the expression for constriction resistance 25, 26 for small contact areas. We show how a contact geometry that is more evenly distributed results in lower impedance compared to a concentrated one for the same contact area due to a more uniform potential distribution.
To complement the experiments, we implemented a finite-element model that incorporates electromagnetic contact conditions and contact loss at the electrode/SE interface. We simulate the experimental geometry using this model which demonstrates strong agreement with the measured EIS and interfacial resistance. Our simulations provide insights into the spatial distribution of potential gradients and their dependence on contact geometry.
![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/x1.png) 
We consider the schematic electrode-SE interface in Fig. 1 and divide it into two regions: recoverable and unrecoverable contact areas. The recoverable region refers to areas where contact can be reestablished or adjusted by applying pressure, allowing for modulation of the contact morphology. The unrecoverable region, on the other hand, represents areas where no contact occurs, and the morphology remains unaffected by pressure. This distinction is critical for understanding and optimizing interfacial contact in SSBs as unrecoverable contact areas involve large interfacial voids which may require pressures much higher than practically feasible values to establish contact14, 15. Measures other than external pressure may be required to mitigate unrecoverable contact losses. We define as the fraction of recoverable (nominal) contact area and as the fraction of real contact area in recoverable regions. depends on pressure and surface roughness. represents the overall fraction of the real contact area with respect to the total nominal area. Experiments were conducted to analyze the effect of varying the recoverable contact area, real contact area (through pressure), and geometrical distribution of contact loss for the same total contact area. After placing the paper on the pellet, a pressure of 180 MPa was applied to establish contact. Following the EIS tests for a specific contact area, the paper was removed, and the bare pellet was re-pressed at the fabrication pressure (375 MPa) to ensure consistent pellet conditions for subsequent tests. Two different pellets were used for experiments involving variation of recoverable contact area and geometrical distribution of contact.

records.full_markdown:
Title: A Self-Decoupling Multimodal Sensor for Enhanced Early Warning of Lithium-Ion Battery Thermal Runaway

URL Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815

Markdown Content:
## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815)Abstract

Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are central to sustainable energy systems but are vulnerable to thermal runaway (TR), necessitating robust safety monitoring. Conventional single-sensor systems cannot decouple the coupled electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical processes, while existing multimodal sensors suffer from signal cross-talk and large footprints in practical applications. Here, we introduce an insect-inspired, self-decoupling multimodal sensor, fabricated via maskless laser direct writing, that leverages distinct sensing mechanisms and orthogonal output signals for simultaneous strain, temperature, and gas detection. The sensor achieves reliable intrinsic decoupling of strain and temperature over 20 to 110°C, along with an independent gas response. Seamlessly integrated onto lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO 4) cells, it captures real-time multimodal data during both normal and TR events. Coupled with a bespoke multiphysics model, this platform reconstructs the thermal–mechanical evolution of LIBs. Our work provides a compact and durable strategy for precise real-time monitoring and early warning of battery failure.

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815)Introduction

Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), endowed with high energy density, long cycle life, and eco-friendly recyclability, are indispensable to the global sustainable energy transition and are extensively deployed in electric vehicles, grid-scale storage systems, and consumer electronics [[1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B1)]. However, under thermal, mechanical, or electrical abuse, these cells can trigger irreversible exothermic chain reactions—thermal runaway (TR) [[2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B2)] process driven by internal chain exothermic reactions under abuse conditions, such as solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) decomposition and separator melting [[3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B3),[4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B4)], is influenced by state of charge (SOC), and high charge/discharge rates markedly increase its hazards [[5](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B5),[6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B6)]. While LIBs are often housed in confined spaces, the flammable gases and high-temperature particles rapidly released during TR can quickly accumulate or disperse [[7](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B7),[8](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B8)]. If subsequently exposed to stimuli such as arc faults or collisions, these conditions can readily trigger fires, explosions, or severe structural damage [[9](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B9)]. To address this risk, beyond passive protection strategies such as developing novel flame-retardant materials and separators [[10](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B10),[11](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B11)], establishing precise TR detection and early warning systems is crucial for enabling timely intervention and ensuring battery system safety [[12](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B12)].

Early investigations focused on single-modality sensing, tracking electrical parameters [[13](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B13)], surface temperature [[14](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B14)], pressure [[15](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B15)], or gas emissions [[16](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B16)] for LIB safety monitoring. Nevertheless, such single-modality monitoring approaches fail to correlate external signals with battery internal reactions, in which electrochemical reactions, heat generation, and mechanical stress interact in complex ways, limiting their ability to comprehensively and accurately define the early warning window of TR [[17](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B17)].

To address these limitations, the concept of multimodal monitoring has emerged. This approach integrates multiple types of sensors to simultaneously monitor key physical parameters during LIB operation. Optical fiber sensors have been explored for LIB safety monitoring. For instance, Huang et al. [[18](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B18)] developed an optical fiber sensor with the capability of decoupling temperature and pressure signals, enabling real-time monitoring of the formation and structural evolution of the SEI layer. Mei et al. [[19](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B19)] integrated both a fiber Bragg grating and an open-cavity Fabry–Pérot interferometer onto a single optical fiber, leveraging their distinct sensitivities to temperature and pressure for intrinsic signal decoupling. However, their accuracy and long-term reliability are challenged during implantation and employment, where bending and vibrations can easily damage the sensors [[20](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B20)]. Moreover, the deployment of optical fiber sensors often relies on auxiliary equipment such as laser sources and fiber Bragg grating demodulators. The bulk and complexity of these systems largely hinder their applicability in practical industrial scenarios.

Thin-film multimodal sensors hold substantial promise for LIB monitoring owing to their superior flexibility, mechanical robustness, customizability, low cost, and portability. Fang’s group [[21](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B21)] developed a thin-film wireless multimodal sensor embedded inside LIBs for real-time state monitoring of strain and temperature. However, the decoupling of multimodal signals in their design does not originate from the intrinsic properties of the sensor itself but is achieved by placing a temperature sensor along a direction orthogonal to the principal strain. For real-time monitoring under electrical TR, Zhang et al. [[22](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B22)] developed a dual-modal sensor that leverages independent piezoresistive and thermoresistive mechanisms for simultaneous temperature and pressure detection.

Despite the aforementioned achievements, implementing multimodal monitoring strategies still presents considerable challenges due to the complex physical–chemical processes occurring within the LIBs. During charge–discharge or abuse conditions, electrode swelling and deformation, rapid temperature fluctuations, and the evolution of gases occur concurrently [[23](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B23)]. These interdependent parameters not only serve as critical indicators of LIB state but also introduce cross-sensitivity issues for multimodal sensors. This signal cross-talk impairs the accurate identification of individual stimuli, frequently requiring complex hardware and computational strategies for signal decoupling [[24](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12929815#B24)], thereby introducing considerable uncertainty into the estimation of the battery’s early warning window. As a result, combining multiple electrical signal types with orthogonal sensing mechanisms might be a promising approach to achieving robust and durable signal decoupling. Furthermore, most existing studies have focused on dual-modal sensing of temperature and pressure, which facilitates the identification of triggering events during TR in LIBs.

Here, inspired by the multimodal sensing capabilities of insects (e.g., bees) in perceiving force, temperature, and gas stimuli, we propose a self-decoupling multimodal sensor for enhanced early warning of LIB TR. Signal cross-talk is intrinsically minimized using distinct sensing

records.full_markdown:
Bipolar plates for the next generation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs): A review of the latest processing methods for unconventional flow channels
Abstract
The rapid, unsustainable depletion of finite fossil fuel resources and their environmental consequences demand the deployment of affordable clean and sustainable energy solutions. Polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) technology is an important pathway in decarbonization of modern energy systems, especially when fueled by high-purity green hydrogen. In PEMFCs, bipolar plates largely determine cell efficiency, longevity, and affordability, which in turn depends on both material selection and design of the embedded flow channels. Conventional manufacturing processes have long been used to fabricate standard bipolar plate designs; however, they are incompatible with unconventional, intricate geometries due to their insufficient resolution and precision in fabrication of fine features, and reliance on multi-step post-processing modifications that limit their design adaptability. This lack of design flexibility impedes the translation of innovative laboratory-scale concepts to industrial-scale production and their practical adoption. In recent years, a growing body of research publications and patent disclosures has reported advanced manufacturing methods, such as additive manufacturing, capable of producing intricate bipolar plate geometries at competitive costs. However, a discussion of these manufacturing approaches, along with an assessment of their scalability and industrial readiness, remains absent in the literature. This study aims to fill this gap. It outlines recent progress and proposes future research directions toward affordable and efficient bipolar plate solutions for advanced PEMFC systems.

1 Introduction
Fossil fuel–based energy sources are the main contributors to the environmental crisis due to the substantial pollutants they emit into the air, water, and soil. These emissions disrupt climate patterns, acidify oceans, contaminate natural resources, and pose health risks [[1](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib1), [2](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib2)]. With global population growth and associated energy demands, reliance on finite fossil resources cannot be sustained. Given their ecological footprint and rapid, unsustainable depletion, a worldwide transition toward renewable and eco-friendly energy solutions is imperative. Renewable energy flows endlessly from natural resources such as solar radiation, flowing water and ocean waves, wind, and the geothermal heat from the Earth crust; these sources are abundant, continuously replenished, and regarded as viable alternatives to conventional energy sources. However, their large-scale integration into power systems remains limited because of their irregular availability and dependence on climatic and seasonal conditions. Thanks to recent progress in energy storage and smart grid technologies, they have covered 29.8% of global electricity production in 2022 [[3](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib6), [4](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib3), [5](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib4)]. Hydrogen energy based on renewables is another way for energy production.
There are several processes available for hydrogen production [[6](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib93)]. At present, about 96% of hydrogen production relies on fossil fuel-based processes, which is commonly referred to as gray hydrogen [[7](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib5)]. Alternative production routes include biomass gasification and water electrolysis. Hydrogen produced by the former is often contaminated with tar and impurities, whereas water electrolysis, typically powered by renewables and nuclear power [[8](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib13), ], produces high-purity hydrogen. This green hydrogen can be consumed in fuel cells to produce electrical energy through electrochemical reactions, and to contribute to the development of low-carbon energy systems [[9](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib42), [10](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib39), [11](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib40), [12](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib41)]. The main types of fuel cells currently being developed are molten carbonate (MCFC) [[13](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib17)], alkaline (AFC) [[14](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib16)], proton exchange membrane (PEMFC) [[15](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib15)], solid oxide (SOFC) [[16](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib14)], direct methanol (DMFC) [[17](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib18)], and phosphoric acid (PAFC) []. Their technical characteristics are listed in Table [1](https://arxiv.org#S1.T1). They are primarily classified by the electrolyte they use. This categorization dictates the electrochemical processes that occur within the cell, the catalysts, the operational temperature, and ultimately application domain. Among them, PEMFCs have been broadly adopted to supply power to residential and commercial buildings, and industrial sites, as portable power sources, and particularly for vehicular applications [, [18](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib19), [19](https://arxiv.org#bib.bib20)].

records.snippet: by A Ghadbane · 2025 · Cited by 14 — Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) represents a promising technology capable of accelerating green hydrogen production and plays a crucial role ...
records.full_markdown:
Abstract
As a key component of the proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE), the porous transport layer (PTL) not only provides mechanical support but also facilitates the supply of reactants to the electrode and the removal of produced gases and ensures efficient electrical and thermal management. Commercially available PTLs are often repurposed for other applications, such as filtration, and are not specifically tailored for PEMWE applications. Given this context, research output on PTL development has increased notably in recent years. Optimized, structured PTLs with preferred properties require applicable, relevant, and convenient diagnostic tools for PTL material development. As such, this work aims to identify and review a wide range of techniques for evaluating developed PTLs, including electrochemical techniques, custom-engineered cells, operando diagnosis, ex situ characterization, and postmortem analysis. By providing detailed information on these characterization techniques, this review aims to catalyze further research and development in the academic and industrial sectors, enhancing the understanding, development, and quality control of PTL components.

1 Introduction
To phase out fossil fuels and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, a clean hydrogen economy has become a strategic global priority. Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) represents a promising technology capable of accelerating green hydrogen production and plays a crucial role in integrating intermittent renewable energy sources such as wind and solar energy into the power grid. Through the power-to-gas approach, the PEMWE addresses power stability challenges arising from the growing number of converter-interfaced renewable sources connected to the grid. Its dynamic operation and quick start-up capabilities enable it to provide frequency support and stabilize the grid, effectively managing the variability of these renewable energy sources [1]. However, challenges such as high production and operational expenses and insufficient durability have become the main barriers to the widespread adoption of this technology.
Currently, the global hydrogen supply predominantly comes from gray hydrogen derived from fossil fuels. However, by 2050, the amount of green hydrogen is projected to increase significantly, potentially constituting 50%–65% of the total supply mix. This shift is driven by the increasing cost competitiveness of renewable energies and electrolyzers, as well as the international pledge to reduce carbon emissions. After 2025, most hydrogen production is expected to be clean [2]. This race toward decarbonizing the hydrogen production industry highlights the importance of technologies such as the PEMWE. Consequently, considerable research and development efforts have been directed toward enhancing PEMWE technologies over the past two decades (Fig. 1a).
Several reviews have addressed different aspects of PEMWE technology. For example, Carmo et al. [3] provided a comprehensive review of the advancements and challenges associated with PEMWE technology. Their work emphasized the critical issues and fundamental aspects of electrocatalysts, critical component materials, fabrication methods for different components, poisoning effects, and advancements in modeling techniques. Shirvanian and Berkel [4] reviewed state-of-the-art and novel advancements in PEMWE technology, emphasizing the challenges faced by each component. They proposed short-term strategies to address performance and durability issues by optimizing current technology through operational adjustments and component modifications. Additionally, Maier et al. [5] conducted an in-depth study on mass transport phenomena in a PEMWE, discussing flow channels, liquid–gas diffusion layers, and proton/water transport in the polymer electrolyte membrane and underscoring the importance of adequate mass transport in PEMWE operation. This paper also reviews a range of diagnostic techniques for evaluating and analyzing mass transport in PEMWE systems. Bernt et al. [6] addressed the challenges in catalyst development, emphasizing the critical need to reduce iridium usage in PEMWEs to enable large-scale applications. Furthermore, the rotating disk electrode method and accelerated stress testing are essential tools for evaluating the activity and durability of the catalyst layer. Tomić et al. [7] addressed the degradation of PEMWE components under constant and dynamic conditions and examined advances in accelerated degradation testing, emphasizing the need for standardized degradation protocols and procedures. Similarly, Feng et al. [8] conducted a comprehensive review of the various degradation mechanisms affecting key components in a PEMWE and summarized different mitigation strategies. These studies underscore the critical role of accelerated stress tests in circumventing the need for lengthy and costly degradation tests. Moreover, Prestat [9] addressed the critical issue of corrosion in PEMWEs with a focus on the BPP and PTL and highlighted the role of titanium and precious metal coatings as state-of-the-art solutions. This review also explored emerging alternatives such as stainless steel with advanced coatings, emphasizing the need for further research on protective coatings and accelerated stress tests to increase the economic viability and durability of PEMWE systems.
The porous transport layer (PTL) is a key component of the PEMWE anode and significantly influences the cell performance and durability. The primary functions of the PTL include providing mechanical support for the catalyst-coated membrane (CCM), transferring electrons, dispatching reactants, and clearing away the produced hydrogen and oxygen [10]. As such, the impact of PTLs on cell performance has three manifestations: (i) impact on the Ohmic resistance due to the bulk resistance, (ii) impact on the electrode performance due to the contact/interfacial resistance, and (iii) impact on the gas/liquid flow from/to the cell due to the material structure, affecting the mass transport of reactants and evolved gases [11]. Given that commercially available PTLs are materials adopted from other applications, e.g., filtration, their structures are not customized for PEMWE applications. This fact has provoked a considerable increase in research aimed at the development and optimization of PTLs for PEMWE use (Fig. 1b).
Research on PTLs in PEMWEs spans a wide range of aspects and approaches, all aimed at understanding, optimizing, and developing this critical component. A pivotal area of this research involves material characterization and performance evaluation. This work includes mechanical assessments to determine properties such as tensile strength and fatigue strength [12], alongside measurements of thermal conductivity [13], electrical resistance, porosity, contact angle [11], and geometric parameters [14,15,16]. Such characterizations yield important insights necessary for the optimization of this key component. Moreover, morphological studies assess the microstructure and surface features of PTLs, offering valuable information regarding degradation issues and performance characteristics [17, 18]. Considerable research has also explored the durability and stability of PTLs in challenging anodic environments characterized by high potentials and acidic media, focusing on the corrosion behavior of coated and uncoated PTLs [9]. Furthermore, understanding the interactions between the PTL and adjacent components, such as the bipolar plate (BPP) and the CCM, is also a subject of study, as it allows a better understanding of catalyst utilization and two-phase flow dynamics within the PEMWE [19,20,21,22,23]. records.title: 电解水制氢的装置(PEM电解槽膜电极)
records.snippet: 电解水制氢装置中的PEM电解槽核心部件包括双极板、膜电极（MEA）、阳极多孔传输层和阴极气体扩散层（GDL）。双极板是核心部件，负责支撑、导电、传热和传质，直接影响电解性能。膜电极由质子交换膜、催化层和扩散层组成，是电池核心组件。阳极多孔传输层采用钛材料，需兼顾导电性、抗氧化性和水汽渗透性，建议使用薄钛烧结体（孔隙率40-70%）。阴极GDL采用碳基材料，允许气体和液体传输，并提供电子传导路径，但碳基GDL不能用于阳极，因阳极反应会导致碳降解，影响电解槽运行。

records.snippet:
1. 问题的提出 氢燃料电池汽车已成为新能源汽车领域的重点发展方向之一，但氢气具有易燃性，一旦发生氢气泄漏，很容易引发严重的安全事故。
氢燃料电池的膜电极是燃料电池电化学反应发生的区域，是整个燃料电池系统的核心部件，由于薄膜针孔或者边框封装等缺陷的存在，可能引发内漏降低效率和形成氢氧界面等问题给电池运行带来严重风险。
通常电池厂家在膜电极装配后会进行气密性检测，但发现泄露发生时难以找出问题膜电极，因此膜电极出厂前应当对每一片膜电极进行漏率检测，找出问题膜电极，保证出厂膜电极质量。
为了保证膜电极漏率检测的准确性和规范性，我国在2020年推出了相应的行业团体标准T/CAAMTB 12-2020《质子交换膜燃料电池膜电极测试方法》。

records.title: 钙钛矿器件——光致发光与电致发光成像
records.snippet: 近年来，有机金属钙钛矿太阳能电池的快速发展推动了柔性、低成本光伏材料的研究。钙钛矿材料因其高载流子迁移率、强吸收能力和可调带隙等特性，成为制造低成本太阳能电池的理想材料。Photon etc.的全局高光谱成像平台（IMA和GRAND-EOS）可快速表征钙钛矿晶体及器件的结构和物理特性，结合光谱与成像技术，可获取光致发光（PL）、电致发光（EL）、透射率和反射率数据，用于分析吸收特性、缺陷、非辐射复合损失、均匀性及衰退行为。结合绝对校准模块，还可提取光电性能参数，如准费米能级分裂、载流子传输效率、开路电压和外量子效率。该平台还可用于光致发光激发（PLE）测量，帮助识别材料不均匀性和非辐射复合损失。研究显示，钙钛矿器件的性能与电子传输层有关，光致发光成像有助于识别缺陷和优化制造工艺。高光谱成像技术在钙钛矿材料研究中广泛应用，有助于深入理解其微观结构和退化机制，推动其向实际应用迈进。

- [EV-CN-065] (CN | T3 | metaso | 2022年06月14日) 电解水制氢的装置(PEM电解槽膜电极)

  Content: 电解水制氢装置中的PEM电解槽核心部件包括双极板、膜电极（MEA）、阳极多孔传输层和阴极气体扩散层（GDL）。双极板是核心部件，负责支撑、导电、传热和传质，直接影响电解性能。膜电极由质子交换膜、催化层和扩散层组成，是电池核心组件。阳极多孔传输层采用钛材料，需兼顾导电性、抗氧化性和水汽渗透性，建议使用薄钛烧结体（孔隙率40-70%）。阴极GDL采用碳基材料，允许气体和液体传输，并提供电子传导路径，但碳基GDL不能用于阳极，因阳极反应会导致碳降解，影响电解槽运行。

  URL: https://www.instrument.com.cn/application/Solution-935720.html
  Content: 1. 问题的提出 氢燃料电池汽车已成为新能源汽车领域的重点发展方向之一，但氢气具有易燃性，一旦发生氢气泄漏，很容易引发严重的安全事故。 氢燃料电池的膜电极是燃料电池电化学反应发生的区域，是整个燃料电池系统的核心部件，由于薄膜针孔或者边框封装等缺陷的存在，可能引发内漏降低效率和形成氢氧界面等问题给电池运行带来严重风险。 通常电池厂家在膜电极装配后会进行气密性检测，但发现泄露发生时难以找出问题膜电极，因此膜电极出厂前应当对每一片膜电极进行漏率检测，找出问题膜电极，保证出厂膜电极质量。 为了保证膜电极漏率检测的准确性和规范性，我国在2020年推出了相应的行业团体标准T/CAAMTB 12-2020《质子交换膜燃料电池膜电极测试方法》。

records.title: 国家标准计划《二氧化碳捕集 第1部分:电厂燃烧后CO2捕集性能评估方法》
records.snippet:
CCUS从工业和能源相关来源捕集二氧化碳，并将其储存在地下的地质构造中。
CCUS可以捕集来自基于含碳燃料的过程（包括发电）的排放，并且是唯一能够直接处理多个工业部门（如水泥生产和肥料生产）排放的技术。
在典型的发电厂中，含碳燃料在锅炉中与空气燃烧以产生蒸汽，从而驱动发电机发电。
来自锅炉或燃气轮机的烟气主要由氮气、二氧化碳、水和氧气等组成。
二氧化碳捕集过程将位于传统杂质控制的下游。
records.full_markdown:
国家标准计划《二氧化碳捕集 第1部分:电厂燃烧后CO2捕集性能评估方法》由 TC207（全国环境管理标准化技术委员会）归口 ，主管部门为国家标准委。
主要起草单位 中国华能集团清洁能源技术研究院有限公司 、中国标准化研究院等 。
| 13 环保、保健和安全 | 
| 13.020 环境保护 | 
| 13.020.40 污染、污染控制和保护 | 
本标准等同采用ISO国际标准：ISO 27919-1:2018。
采标中文名称:与电厂集成的燃烧后二氧化碳捕集性能评估方法。
在碳中和目标下，二氧化碳捕集利用与封存技术（CCUS）是实现化石能源低碳化利用的唯一技术选择，是实现碳中和目标的重要技术保障和不可或缺的关键性技术之一。
为了实现缓解气候变化的目标，减少大气二氧化碳排放尤为重要。
将CCUS技术纳入各种可用的减排方法中，可以提高使用全球经济最低成本实现这些目标的可能性。
CCUS从工业和能源相关来源捕集二氧化碳，并将其储存在地下的地质构造中。
CCUS可以捕集来自基于含碳燃料的过程（包括发电）的排放，并且是唯一能够直接处理多个工业部门（如水泥生产和肥料生产）排放的技术。
在典型的发电厂中，含碳燃料在锅炉中与空气燃烧以产生蒸汽，从而驱动发电机发电。
来自锅炉或燃气轮机的烟气主要由氮气、二氧化碳、水和氧气等组成。
二氧化碳捕集过程将位于传统杂质控制的下游。
随着CCUS技术在全球的研究及示范的进展，对该项技术规范和标准的要求被日益关注。
与电厂集成的燃烧后二氧化碳捕集性能评估方法是CCUS标准化领域的一项重要工作。
制定燃烧后二氧化碳捕集性能评估标准有助于规范和统一CCUS领域的装置性能通用基础，有助于各个利益相关方确定不同设备组件的潜在效率改进，指导碳捕集装置性能评估方法的选择，并作为制定法规的资源。
本标准指定了对与发电厂集成的燃烧后捕集装置的性能进行测量、评估和报告的指南，规定了一种计算燃烧后捕集装置具体关键性能指标（KPI）的通用方法，需要定义典型系统的边界以及确定 KPI所需的测量工作。 本标准适用于燃用含碳燃料（如煤、石油、天然气和生物质衍生燃料）的火电厂；本标准所适用的燃烧后捕集技术为基于使用反应性液体（如胺水溶液、碳酸钾溶液和氨水）的化学吸附技术。本标准仅限于基于液体的化学吸附过程的发电厂燃烧后捕集（PCC）的能量需求。 主要技术内容包括: —术语、定义和符号； —与燃烧后捕集装置有关的系统边界定义； —基本燃烧后捕集装置性能的定义； —燃烧后捕集装置的公用工程定义和消耗计算； —燃烧后捕集装置性能评估依据及指导原则； —对要安装或使用的仪表的要求以及推荐的测量方法； —与发电厂集成的燃烧后捕集装置的过程关键性能指标评估；

records.title: 华能正宁电厂150万吨/年二氧化碳捕集、利用与封存（CCUS）示范工程
records.snippet:
这也是一条精益求精之路。
在工程推进过程中，研发团队总在打磨细节：面对复合式吸收塔结构复杂、焊接量大、高空作业面紧张的挑战，通过多次试验，推出“外钢架、筒体、内件分层循环流水作业”模式，保证了一万余次安全起吊；为了验证“捕碳+调峰”协同运行的技术可行性，他们连续多天守在集控室，盯着运行参数界面，不断调整装置参数，直至装置运行技术指标满足设计要求，可随煤电机组运行情况动态调整碳捕集系统负荷。
这还是一条敢于试错的优化之路。
records.full_markdown:
中央纪委国家监委网站 陈瑶
重要论述：我们率先开发风电、光伏,走的路现在看是有前瞻性的,同时,煤电是我们能源的家底,是要发挥托底作用的。一定要坚持走清洁、低碳发展的路子。
春天的陇东大地，生机盎然。甘肃庆阳的正宁电厂内，1号、2号机组稳定运行，源源不断的电能经电网送往千家万户与生产一线。
正宁电厂是国家重大能源通道“陇电入鲁”工程的重要配套调峰电源，承担着筑牢区域电力保供防线、保障能源安全稳定供应的重任。这里有个“碳捕手”，即去年9月正式投运的全球规模最大煤电碳捕集示范工程——华能正宁电厂150万吨/年二氧化碳捕集、利用与封存（CCUS）示范工程（以下简称“正宁电厂示范工程”）。通过“碳捕手”，煤炭燃烧时产生的二氧化碳在吸收塔和再生塔内与吸收剂进行化学反应，从而被捕集，之后再被利用与封存。这一工程，可推动陇东优质煤炭资源实现高效清洁利用、就地转化增值。
CCUS是实现“双碳”目标的核心关键技术之一。自2021年以来，我国CCUS产业加速布局、规模持续扩容。乘着行业发展的东风，正宁电厂示范工程凭借哪些硬核实力脱颖而出？这份服务国家“双碳”战略目标与煤电绿色转型的方案，又蕴含着怎样的时代意义？带着这些问题，记者采访了中国华能集团清洁能源技术研究院有限公司（以下简称“华能清能院”）正宁电厂示范工程研发团队，在对话中探寻“中国方案”的创新密码。
破局突围：从跟跑到引领，助力煤电低碳发展
能源是国民经济的命脉，能源保障与安全直接关系国计民生，关乎发展全局。作为世界上最大的能源生产国和消费国，我国维护能源安全的坚实底气，一方面源自煤炭、石油、天然气、非化石能源等一次能源的综合供给能力，另一方面则得益于发展方式绿色转型取得的扎实成效。
立足我国富煤、贫油、少气的资源禀赋，煤电凭借稳定可靠、调峰能力突出的优势，在当前及今后较长时期内，仍将承担“基础保障+系统调节”的重要功能。但与此同时，煤电行业碳排放总量偏大的现实，也迫切要求加快低碳化改造步伐，纵深推进能源绿色低碳转型。
“实现‘双碳’目标，既要大力构建新型能源体系，也要推动传统能源主动担当作为，探索出一条切实可行的低碳发展路径。”华能清能院院长肖平表示。
煤电作为电力系统的“压舱石”，必须在牢牢守住能源安全底线的前提下推进绿色转型，绝非简单的“去煤化”，而是要全力攻克“用煤不排碳”这一关键技术难关。CCUS正是攻克难关的重要抓手。
放眼全球，欧美在CCUS技术研发与应用领域起步较早。1972年，美国二氧化碳年捕集规模便达到40万至50万吨；20世纪90年代起，欧洲聚焦二氧化碳封存技术，陆续建成一批示范工程。进入21世纪，在应对气候变化的共识下，CCUS作为核心减碳技术受到各国高度重视，我国也加快布局。
在发展初期，我国CCUS发展面临技术“封锁”、装备依赖进口、关键材料受制于人等困境。我国在引进、消化、吸收的基础上逐步追赶，为后续突破积蓄了坚实力量。历经二十余年深耕，我国煤电领域的CCUS项目从每年捕集3000吨提升至50万吨，并迈向自主研发、成熟应用。
“经过这段‘技术长跑’，我们有更足的信心、更强的实力给出CCUS的‘中国方案’。”对于华能清能院副总工程师、温室气体减排部主任郜时旺及其团队来说，这个方案的目标清晰而坚定。
在规模上，实现从“跟随”走向“引领”的转变。在正宁电厂示范工程建成之前，我国在燃煤电厂百万吨级碳捕集示范工程方面存在空白。“中国作为全球煤电装机规模最大的国家，必须打造属于自己的百万吨级‘母舰’，推动碳捕集示范项目从‘十万吨级试验’向‘百万吨级工业化应用’跨越。”郜时旺说。作为全球规模最大煤电碳捕集示范工程，正宁电厂示范工程每年可捕集的二氧化碳量，相当于60万辆汽车一年的碳排放量，可助力燃煤电厂实现大规模、工业化深度减排，推动煤电绿色清洁发展，助推碳中和目标实现。
在装备上，要实现从“引进”到“自主”的跨越。“核心装备100%国产化”“不能让人‘卡脖子’”，每每谈及自主研发，郜时旺的语气不自觉地变得高亢。他说，无论是全球首创的“二塔合一”复合式吸收塔，还是填补国内空白的八级超临界二氧化碳压缩机，唯有实现完全国产化，才能真正筑牢发展底气。
在系统集成上，则要追求“捕碳”与“调峰”的协同。这是正宁电厂示范工程区别于国际同类项目的一大亮点。在郜时旺眼中，团队打造的并非单一环保设备，而是可与电网深度融合的“智慧型”碳捕集系统。该系统能够动态调整负荷，使煤电机组在高效捕集二氧化碳的同时，灵活适配电网调度需求，切实保障电力供应安全稳定。
攻坚破难：在“无人区”蹚路，锻造自主创新硬核实力
2026年，从正宁电厂燃煤机组捕集到的二氧化碳，被注入地下3000米深的咸水层进行永久地质封存。这是正宁电厂示范工程正式运行后取得的阶段性成果。
成果令人欣喜，背后的攻坚克难、精益求精值得回味。
“正宁电厂示范工程的每一步，都是在为未来探索一条可行的减排路径。”坚守这份信念，研发团队为正宁电厂示范工程设定了几个核心指标，其中之一是二氧化碳纯度达99%以上。
99%，意味着近乎纯净的产品品质。经碳捕集系统处理后的二氧化碳，纯度达到99%以上，这意味着它不再是工业废气，而是可以进入化工合成甚至精密焊接领域的资源。
记者了解到，捕集率越高，往往能耗越高；要求纯度达到99%，核心装备必须过硬，自主创新是唯一的出路。
“以前我们更多是在跟踪国际前沿，看别人怎么做、学别人怎么做。但核心技术买不来，更何况在这个工程中，我们面对的是全球最大规模、没有任何成熟经验可照搬的‘无人区’，只能靠自己干。”华能清能院温室气体减排部副主任牛红伟告诉记者，从27层楼高的“二塔合一”复合式吸收塔的设计，到八级超临界二氧化碳压缩机的攻关，再到深部咸水层多层封存体系的构建，“每一天都在面对未知，每一个环节都在逼自己蹚出一条路。”
这是一条啃硬骨头的研发之路。以八级超临界二氧化碳压缩机为例，它是负责加压输送二氧化碳的动力“心脏”。研发团队调研发现，当时国际上能生产此类压缩机的厂家屈指可数，而且对中国实行技术封锁；国内最高只能做到六级压缩，无法满足大规模、长距离二氧化碳传输与利用需求。困境之下，研发团队与设备厂家从基础研究做起，从材料、转子动力学到流道设计，一步步啃硬骨头，先后攻克了多级高速复杂轴系稳定性、窄流道三元闭式叶轮加工等一系列技术难关，最终设计出国内首台八级超临界二氧化碳压缩机，为捕集后二氧化碳大规模管道输送与封存提供了重要设备支撑。
这也是一条精益求精之路。在工程推进过程中，研发团队总在打磨细节：面对复合式吸收塔结构复杂、焊接量大、高空作业面紧张的挑战，通过多次试验，推出“外钢架、筒体、内件分层循环流水作业”模式，保证了一万余次安全起吊；为了验证“捕碳+调峰”协同运行的技术可行性，他们连续多天守在集控室，盯着运行参数界面，不断调整装置参数，直至装置运行技术指标满足设计要求，可随煤电机组运行情况动态调整碳捕集系统负荷。
这还是一条敢于试错的优化之路。“实验室里的技术再成熟，只有通过真实、复杂的燃煤烟气验证，才能从样品变成产品，最终推向市场变成商品。”令牛红伟印象深刻的是建设调试阶段的一次次试验，“从实验室到工厂，小试成功的工艺，在放大百倍千倍后，因流体的分布、传质传热的效率会发生巨大变化，很可能达不到目标值，甚至会出现致命缺陷。”研发过程中，无数次失败让大家深切体会到科研不是一帆风顺的坦途，而是布满荆棘的攀登。但也正是在一次次推倒重来中，正宁电厂示范工程的“二塔合一”复合式吸收塔空间利用率变得更高、结构性能变得更优，自主研发的二氧化碳捕集吸收剂突破了再生能耗高、降解严重的难题，关键技术指标达到国际领先水平。
向绿而行：聚力迭代优化，续写低碳转型篇章
正宁电厂示范工程的正式投运，其意义不仅在于验证了我国CCUS技术的成熟可靠性，更在于向全球碳减排领域递上了一份兼具实力与温度的“中国方案”：
一套“全链条自主创新，核心装备100%国产化”的技术装备体系，从此任何国家想发展CCUS，都多了一个“中国选项”；
一种“煤电低碳转型+能源安全保障”协同发展的系统范式，证明了能源转型可以通过技术创新，实现发展与减排的平衡；
一条“产学研用协同、创新联合体攻关”的产业培育路径，有效整合了碳捕集、输送、利用、封存全链条资源，凝聚起多方力量，合力把CCUS产业链的“蛋糕”做大、做优、做扎实，为产业高质量发展筑牢根基。
随着工程的投运，研发团队再次忙碌起来，向着更高目标稳步迈进。
“站在新的起点，我们的工作重心将从‘建设攻坚’向‘运维优化、迭代升级’阶段推进。”华能清能院温室气体减排部刘汉明博士告诉记者。
运维优化阶段，核心目标是让整套装置“跑得更稳、更省、更高效”。投运之后，研发团队的首要任务便是持续优化运行参数，全面验证装置长周期稳定运行的可靠性。“我们将在实际运行中精准验证每一组数据，不断优化吸收剂配方、降低再生能耗，力争让这套系统的能耗再降一步、效率再提一截，充分释放技术潜力。”刘汉明补充道。
当前CCUS面临的最大瓶颈是成本。到了迭代升级阶段，就要通过规模化示范，让技术“成本更低、竞争力更强”。记者获悉，团队将在高效、低能耗二氧化碳吸收剂研发领域持续攻坚，突破关键技术瓶颈；同时，将以正宁电厂为核心枢纽，积极探索与周边油田、化工企业的深度协同模式，逐步构建起“碳捕集—资源化—收益反哺”的商业闭环，让CCUS真正从“可行”走向“可持续”。
展望未来，CCUS是一个需要长期坚守的方向，征途注定不是一马平川，需要耐得住寂寞、扛得住压力、经得起波折。只有以勇敢为翼、以恒心为伴，才能在绿色转型的战场上破局而立，书写属于这一代科研工作者的硬核答卷。
记者手记丨最动人心是情怀
在正宁电厂，示范工程的成效闪烁着耀眼光芒，同样闪亮的还有一群平凡科研工作者的奋斗历程。他们幽默又鲜活，将碳捕集过程中二氧化碳与吸收剂的反应巧作比喻：吸收塔是“淋浴间”，燃煤产生的烟气从“淋浴间”下端涌入；吸收剂是特制的“洗澡水”，从塔顶喷淋而下，“能像磁铁吸铁屑一样，只把二氧化碳‘抓’进液体里，而让洁净的烟气排出”。这份鲜活背后，是对科研的热爱与对生活的细致观察。
最打动人的，是他们藏在坚守里的家国情怀。“心中装着‘国之大者’”“必须走通‘中国路’”，一句句真挚话语，道出了科研工作者20年坚守不变的初心，也彰显了突破国外技术封锁的决心。
微光虽小，照亮前行路；逐光而行，路虽远行则将至。从技术跟跑到引领，从工程投运到迭代优化，扎根一线的科研人，以初心为炬，怀揣信念、坚韧不拔，在CCUS“无人区”默默探索，终破壁垒，不仅为煤电低碳转型交出了亮眼的中国答卷，更向世界传递了中国科研工作者的执着与担当。（陈瑶）

records.title: DFT study of atmospheric characteristics of CF3SO2F - PMC
records.snippet: by W Liu · 2026 · Cited by 2 — The GWP of CF3SO2F (4320) is significantly lower than that of SF6 (22 845), indicating that CF3SO2F is a promising and environmentally friendly alternative gas ...
records.full_markdown:
Title: DFT study of atmospheric characteristics of CF3SO2F: the fungibility of the insulation gas of SF6

URL Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281

Markdown Content:
## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281)Abstract

Due to the significant greenhouse effect of SF 6, CF 3 SO 2 F has emerged as a potential alternative that meets the requirements for insulation gases in high-voltage electrical equipment. Herein, the atmospheric lifetime and global warming potential (GWP) of CF 3 SO 2 F were evaluated based on its interactions with hydroxide radicals (·OH) using theoretical calculations. By employing the Monte Carlo method, we constructed molecular structures of SF 6–H 2 O and CF 3 SO 2 F–H 2 O as mixed-gas systems to simulate the dissociation of these insulation gases under atmospheric conditions. The adversative efficiency (RE) of CF 3 SO 2 F was determined to be 0.177 W (m 2 ppbv)−1, with an atmospheric lifetime of 52.02 years and a GWP of 4320. The reactive models, developed using density functional theory (DFT) and Car–Parrinello molecular dynamics (CPMD), not only enable the determination of the dissociation pathway in the atmosphere, but also provide detailed insights into the interactions with ·OH based on the overall dynamic behaviour.

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281)Abstract

The possible dissociation of SF 3 SO 2 F under atmospheric conditions (·OH) is simulated by Car–Parrinello molecular dynamics (CPMD), and its global warming potential (GWP) value is evaluated by theoretical calculations.

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281)Introduction

1.
SF 6 plays an essential role in the power industry due to its excellent dielectric strength, heat transfer capability, and arc-quenching ability.[1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit1) Toxic decomposition products can be formed from SF 6 under electric arc conditions, despite the gas itself being non-toxic.[2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit2) SF 6 is a potent greenhouse gas with a 100 year global warming potential (GWP100) of 23 500, equivalent to 23 500 kg CO 2 per kg of SF 6, and an atmospheric lifetime of approximately 3200 years.[3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit3) Global emissions of SF 6 have been increasing, reaching 9040 tons in 2018, with the power industry accounting for 80% of this total. Consequently, atmospheric concentrations of SF 6 have risen from 0.66 parts per trillion (ppt) by volume in 1978 to over 11 ppt in 2022.[4,5](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit4) Faced with this rapid accumulation and its permanent climate impact, aggressively implementing mitigation strategies and switching to sustainable alternatives is an urgent priority. Over the past decades, great efforts have been devoted to identifying such replacements, and several potential alternatives were reported, including C 5 F 10 O and C 3 F 7 CN.[6,7](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit6) However, these gases often suffer from drawbacks, such as high liquefaction temperatures and potential toxicity. Furthermore, despite having potentially superior dielectric strength and lower GWP values than SF 6, their GWP values are still relatively high, limiting their applicability as environmentally friendly insulation media.[8,9](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit8)

CF 3 SO 2 F has attracted considerable attention as a promising replacement for SF 6 due to its excellent insulation performance, low boiling point of −22 °C, and low GWP value.[10–15](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit10) Studies of field-dependent electron–molecule capture rates suggest that CF 3 SO 2 F possesses a higher dielectric strength than SF 6.[9](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit9) Both theoretical and experimental investigations have confirmed that the thermal stability of CF 3 SO 2 F is comparable to that of SF 6.[15](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit15) Furthermore, CF 3 SO 2 F has been demonstrated to exhibit a short atmospheric lifetime and a minimal contribution to smog formation,[16](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit16) along with a higher breakdown voltage (32 kV) than that of SF 6 (26 kV).[17](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit17) These properties collectively suggest that it is more environmentally friendly and suitable for replacing SF 6 in electrical equipment. Although its boiling point is higher than that of SF 6 (−63.8 °C), its strong dielectric strength and high thermal stability make it applicable in most geographical regions.[12](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit12) Zhang _et al._ reported that CF 3 SO 2 F mainly decomposes _via_ C–S bond cleavage, yielding CF 3 and SO 2 F radicals. These radicals can further react with free F radicals to form CF 4 and SO 2. Alternatively, decomposition can proceed through CF 3 migration and memorization, forming the more stable intermediate CF 3 OSFO, which subsequently decomposes into CF 2 O and SOF 2.[18](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit18) Wang's team has conducted an in-depth analysis of CF 3 SO 2 F decomposition products.[19](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit19)

The atmospheric behavior and ultimate fate of an insulation gas are directly determined by its reactivity under atmospheric conditions. The most reliable method for estimating the lifetime of a trace gas involves chemical transport models (CTMs), which require accurate rate constants for reactions with ·OH as critical input parameters.[13](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12869281#cit13) For chemically reactive trace gases, atmospheric degradation by ·OH is often the dominant process governing their global atmospheric lifetime. Therefore, to evaluate the environmental impact of the insulation gas SF 6 and its alternatives, it is essential to establish a systematic model that simulates atmospheric dissociation based on structure–property relationships. Constructing such mixed-gas models is necessary to fully elucidate the atmospheric interaction mechanisms between insulation gases and ·OH.

In this work, we first compared the electronic structures and RE of SF 6 and CF 3 SO 2 F based on their optimized molecular geometries. Given that ·OH plays a key role as a reactive species interacting with greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, a co-crystal structure of CF 3 SO 2 F and H 2 O with a 1 : 1 molar ratio was constructed using the MC method. The complete set of four dissociation pathways of CF 3 SO 2 F with ·OH in the atmosphere was revealed through Car–Parrinello molecular dynamics (CPMD) simulations. Based on the analysis of the reaction pathways, reaction rates, atmospheric lifetime, and GWP were calculated. The combined computational framework of density functional theory (DFT) and CPMD established in this study provides a reliable basis for systematically evaluating the atmospheric behavior of these gases and screening potential alternatives to SF 6.

records.title: 基于可调谐激光技术的C<sub>4</sub>F<sub>7</sub>N气体中微水含量检测装置的研制
records.snippet: 本文介绍了基于可调谐激光技术的C4F7N气体中微水含量检测装置的研制。C4F7N是一种替代SF6的环保绝缘气体，其在高压设备中使用时，水分含量超标会导致设备放电和绝缘性能下降。因此，研发针对C4F7N的微水检测设备具有重要意义。本文研究了可调谐激光红外吸收光谱法对C4F7N中微水含量的定量检测技术，包括光谱理论、谐波检测原理和水分的红外吸收特性。设计了TDLAS结构，选用DFB激光器，制作光电转换模块、光源驱动模块、红外多次反射池及电路和软件部分，研制出检测装置，可检测至1 μL/L的低限值。实验结果表明，装置性能满足标准要求，检测精度高，有助于准确判断设备运行状态。

records.title: 基于NDIR技术的微量环保绝缘气体C<sub>4</sub>F<sub>7</sub>N检测
records.snippet:
文中通过红外光谱平台，确定了C4F7N的红外光谱信息。
通过对C4F7N体积分数为100~2 000 μL/L的C4F7N/CO2混合气体检测，确定了微量C4F7N的最佳检测波段。
搭建了基于NDIR技术的微量C4F7N检测平台，测量通道滤光片为7.9 μm，实现了对12.6~52.5 μL/L的微量C4F7N定量检测，C4F7N气体体积分数与反演信号值的线性拟合系数R2为0.989，最大绝对误差为0.107。
研究成果为C4F7N/CO2混合气体绝缘设备的绝缘状态评估提供了一种可行方案。

records.title: C4F7N和CO2混合气体在高压电气设备中的应用研究
records.snippet:
光谱法利用每种气体分子有特定吸收光谱的特性，其吸收强度与浓度符合朗伯-比尔（Beer-Lambert）定律。
通过对绝缘气体的检测方法对比得出：气相色谱法不适于现场监测，取样周期长，难以实施在线监测；对C4F7N气体性质进行初步研究发现，C4F7N气体的热导率与其混合气体的别一种成份CO2的热导率非常相近，使用热导原理精度与灵敏度很低，无法达到指标要求。
而C4F7N由于C—F键的存在，在1400~730 cm-1波长范围内具有强的红外吸收，容易辨识，非常适合红外光谱检测技术的应用。
因此，采用红外光谱对C4F7N和CO2混合气体进行在线检测成为目前研究的主流。

records.title: Detection of decomposition products of C4F7N-CO2 gas mixture based on infrared spectroscopy
records.snippet: 本文研究了基于红外光谱检测C4F7N-CO2混合气体分解产物的可行性。C4F7N-CO2混合气体作为一种优良的环保绝缘介质，其分解特性研究有助于理解其在绝缘故障下的分解机理，并为基于分解产物分析监测电气设备绝缘状态提供依据。红外光谱在电气设备在线监测中具有潜力，因此本文探讨了其检测分解产物的可行性。通过理论计算获得了C4F7N及其分解产物的红外光谱，并分析了红外光谱检测的可能性。搭建了C4F7N-CO2混合气体过热分解实验平台，研制了4m光程长路径气室，用于痕量分解产物的检测。结果表明，C3F6、COF2和CO可通过红外光谱与长路径气室有效检测。最后，进行了不同温度和压力下的分解实验，分析了分解产物的增长趋势。研究证实了红外光谱法检测C4F7N-CO2混合气体分解产物的可行性，为未来基于红外光谱的混合气体电气设备在线监测技术奠定了基础。

records.title: 华能清能院CCUS团队研发出多种二氧化碳吸收剂及捕集塔填料等
records.snippet:
调整压力值、设定温度参数……走进实验室，记者看到CCUS团队成员李野正在一个一人多高、两米多长的装置前进行实验操作。
“这就是二氧化碳捕集实验装置。”李野告诉记者。
该实验装置是这样工作的：模拟火电厂、化工厂、水泥厂或者钢铁厂等“排放大户”排出的、经过预处理的烟气，经过两个又细又高的塔状设备处理，便可实现二氧化碳的捕集和再生，二氧化碳的捕集率可超过90%。
“烟气经过第一个塔时，二氧化碳会被吸收剂吸收;经过第二个塔时，在高温状态下，实现吸收剂与二氧化碳的分离再生。”

records.title: 亚洲最大火电碳捕集利用与封存（CCUS）项目——国家能源集团江苏泰州电厂项目正式投产
records.snippet: 国家能源集团江苏泰州电厂项目正式投产，成为亚洲最大火电碳捕集利用与封存（CCUS）项目。该项目每年可捕集50万吨二氧化碳，用于工业、食品等领域，实现资源再利用。捕集过程通过水洗塔、吸收塔、再生塔完成，二氧化碳纯度超99%。项目捕集率超90%，具备环保与商业价值。目前二氧化碳主要用于工业和食品领域，市场调研确保其商用价值。项目通过技术创新降低成本，提高效率，为CCUS大规模应用提供参考。在“双碳”目标下，CCUS行业前景广阔，未来需加大技术攻关，推动商业化应用。

- [EV-CN-083] (CN | T1 | metaso | 2023年09月28日) 国家标准计划《二氧化碳捕集 第1部分:电厂燃烧后CO2捕集性能评估方法》
  URL: https://std.samr.gov.cn/gb/search/gbDetailed?id=CB62BCD722B3DD18E05397BE0A0AA94E
  Content: 国家标准计划《二氧化碳捕集 第1部分:电厂燃烧后CO2捕集性能评估方法》由 TC207（全国环境管理标准化技术委员会）归口 ，主管部门为国家标准委。 主要起草单位 中国华能集团清洁能源技术研究院有限公司 、中国标准化研究院等 。 | 13 环保、保健和安全 |  | 13.020 环境保护 |  | 13.020.40 污染、污染控制和保护 |  本标准等同采用ISO国际标准：ISO 27919-1:2018。 采标中文名称:与电厂集成的燃烧后二氧化碳捕集性能评估方法。 在碳中和目标下，二氧化碳捕集利用与封存技术（CCUS）是实现化石能源低碳化利用的唯一技术选择，是实现碳中和目标的重要技术保障和不可或缺的关键性技术之一。 为了实现缓解气候变化的目标，减少大气二氧化碳排放尤为重要。 将CCUS技术纳入各种可用的减排方法中，可以提高使用全球经济最低成本实现这些目标的可能性。 CCUS从工业和能源相关来源捕集二氧化碳，并将其储存在地下的地质构造中。 CCUS可以捕集来自基于含碳燃料的过程（包括发电）的排放，并且是唯一能够直接处理多个工业部门（如水泥生产和肥料生产）排放的技术。 在典型的发电厂中，含碳燃料在锅炉中与空气燃烧以产生蒸汽，从而驱动发电机发电。 来自锅炉或燃气轮机的烟气主要由氮气、二氧化碳、水和氧气等组成。 二氧化碳捕集过程将位于传统杂质控制的下游。 随着CCUS技术在全球的研究及示范的进展，对该项技术规范和标准的要求被日益关注。 与电厂集成的燃烧后二氧化碳捕集性能评估方法是CCUS标准化领域的一项重要工作。 制定燃烧后二氧化碳捕集性能评估标准有助于规范和统一CCUS领域的装置性能通用基础，有助于各个利益相关方确定不同设备组件的潜在效率改进，指导碳捕集装置性能评估方法的选择，并作为制定法规的资源。 本标准指定了对与发电厂集成的燃烧后捕集装置的性能进行测量、评估和报告的指南，规定了一种计算燃烧后捕集装置具体关键性能指标（KPI）的通用方法，需要定义典型系统的边界以及确定 KPI所需的测量工作。 本标准适用于燃用含碳燃料（如煤、石油、天然气和生物质衍生燃料）的火电厂；本标
- [EV-CN-084] (CN | T1 | metaso | 2026年01月01日) 华能正宁电厂150万吨/年二氧化碳捕集、利用与封存（CCUS）示范工程
  URL: http://www.fcqjw.gov.cn/publish/cbnews/202604/20/cb18006_1.shtml
  Content: 中央纪委国家监委网站 陈瑶 重要论述：我们率先开发风电、光伏,走的路现在看是有前瞻性的,同时,煤电是我们能源的家底,是要发挥托底作用的。一定要坚持走清洁、低碳发展的路子。 春天的陇东大地，生机盎然。甘肃庆阳的正宁电厂内，1号、2号机组稳定运行，源源不断的电能经电网送往千家万户与生产一线。 正宁电厂是国家重大能源通道“陇电入鲁”工程的重要配套调峰电源，承担着筑牢区域电力保供防线、保障能源安全稳定供应的重任。这里有个“碳捕手”，即去年9月正式投运的全球规模最大煤电碳捕集示范工程——华能正宁电厂150万吨/年二氧化碳捕集、利用与封存（CCUS）示范工程（以下简称“正宁电厂示范工程”）。通过“碳捕手”，煤炭燃烧时产生的二氧化碳在吸收塔和再生塔内与吸收剂进行化学反应，从而被捕集，之后再被利用与封存。这一工程，可推动陇东优质煤炭资源实现高效清洁利用、就地转化增值。 CCUS是实现“双碳”目标的核心关键技术之一。自2021年以来，我国CCUS产业加速布局、规模持续扩容。乘着行业发展的东风，正宁电厂示范工程凭借哪些硬核实力脱颖而出？这份服务国家“双碳”战略目标与煤电绿色转型的方案，又蕴含着怎样的时代意义？带着这些问题，记者采访了中国华能集团清洁能源技术研究院有限公司（以下简称“华能清能院”）正宁电厂示范工程研发团队，在对话中探寻“中国方案”的创新密码。 破局突围：从跟跑到引领，助力煤电低碳发展 能源是国民经济的命脉，能源保障与安全直接关系国计民生，关乎发展全局。作为世界上最大的能源生产国和消费国，我国维护能源安全的坚实底气，一方面源自煤炭、石油、天然气、非化石能源等一次能源的综合供给能力，另一方面则得益于发展方式绿色转型取得的扎实成效。 立足我国富煤、贫油、少气的资源禀赋，煤电凭借稳定可靠、调峰能力突出的优势，在当前及今后较长时期内，仍将承担“基础保障+系统调节”的重要功能。但与此同时，煤电行业碳排放总量偏大的现实，也迫切要求加快低碳化改造步伐，纵深推进能源绿色低碳转型。 “实现‘双碳’目标，既要大力构建新型能源体系，也要推动传统能源主动担当作为，探索出一条切实可行的低碳发展路径。”华
- [EV-CN-077] (CN | T3 | metaso | 2024年08月01日) 基于可调谐激光技术的C<sub>4</sub>F<sub>7</sub>N气体中微水含量检测装置的研制
  URL: https://doaj.org/article/49e30c2541a14f7d90135c8e1ce59c6a
  Content: 本文介绍了基于可调谐激光技术的C4F7N气体中微水含量检测装置的研制。C4F7N是一种替代SF6的环保绝缘气体，其在高压设备中使用时，水分含量超标会导致设备放电和绝缘性能下降。因此，研发针对C4F7N的微水检测设备具有重要意义。本文研究了可调谐激光红外吸收光谱法对C4F7N中微水含量的定量检测技术，包括光谱理论、谐波检测原理和水分的红外吸收特性。设计了TDLAS结构，选用DFB激光器，制作光电转换模块、光源驱动模块、红外多次反射池及电路和软件部分，研制出检测装置，可检测至1 μL/L的低限值。实验结果表明，装置性能满足标准要求，检测精度高，有助于准确判断设备运行状态。

  Content: 光谱法利用每种气体分子有特定吸收光谱的特性，其吸收强度与浓度符合朗伯-比尔（Beer-Lambert）定律。 通过对绝缘气体的检测方法对比得出：气相色谱法不适于现场监测，取样周期长，难以实施在线监测；对C4F7N气体性质进行初步研究发现，C4F7N气体的热导率与其混合气体的别一种成份CO2的热导率非常相近，使用热导原理精度与灵敏度很低，无法达到指标要求。 而C4F7N由于C—F键的存在，在1400~730 cm-1波长范围内具有强的红外吸收，容易辨识，非常适合红外光谱检测技术的应用。 因此，采用红外光谱对C4F7N和CO2混合气体进行在线检测成为目前研究的主流。

records.snippet: by KS Chen · 2026 · Cited by 1 — Thermo-mechanical mismatch induced bifurcation warpage in wafer level packaging could strongly impact the process and device reliability. Such a concern should ...
records.full_markdown:
Abstract
Fan-out wafer level packages (FOWLP) have been widely used in IC packaging industries but the associated asymmetric warpage in the process may affect the process integrity and final product yields. Such a concern should be reduced through proper design based on adequate analysis and efficient and process simulation. The full-scale FEM simulations, although accurate, are inadequate for early-stage design analysis due to high computational cost. In this work, essential semi-analytical models for bifurcation prediction and efficient process emulators are developed to fully address the needs by modeling a comprehensive reconstituted wafer as a bi-layer-equivalent anisotropic structure for estimating key performances index such as bifurcation temperatures and processing warpages. Various material equivalence models are compared, and their effectiveness and accuracy have been evaluated and the virtual tensile testing approach is finally adapted. In comparison with the corresponding fully 3D FEM, the simplified model shows that a slight sacrifice on the achieved accuracy could reduce computational cost significantly based on the same hardware and this implies that a more thoughtful software DOE could be conducted for design optimization in the future. Subsequently, the standard chip-first and chip-last process emulators are then developed for predicting the wafer warping behavior throughout the entire processing and to perform parametric study to elucidate the applications of this work in packaging design analysis.
Similar content being viewed by others
1 Introduction
Fan-out wafer level packages (FOWLP) have become increasingly popular and mature in electronic packaging industries for both IC and MEMS. By reconstituting chips with molding compounds as well as other components such as micro bumps and metal layers, it is designed to provide increased I/O density at a lower cost, as well as exceptional electrical performance and heterogeneous integration capabilities [1,2,3,4,5] to bridge the gap between front-end and back-end microelectronics processes. However, several technical challenges and problems generally occurred in the FOWLP impacting structural reliability. In particular, wafer warpage induced due to mismatching in coefficients of thermal expansion (CTEs) from various materials during temperature cycles in processing is a traditional annoying issue. How to reduce process-induced warpage is a major issue in virtually all wafer-level packaging processing.
Furthermore, under sufficient high stress, asymmetric warping has been observed due to structurally nonlinearity or buckling [6, 7]. Figure 1 shows typical finite element out of plane deformation contours to illustrate the difference between symmetric and asymmetric warping. Readers are encouraged to refer [8] to the real asymmetric deformation example. Such excessive warpage and bifurcation may impose further concerns in subsequent processing in wafer handling and surface measurements, as well as on structural reliability degradations. Since wafer warpage is mainly caused by thermo-mechanical mismatch of device materials during processing, where the material properties, chip layout, processing parameters, and handling manners are key influence factors, comprehensive analyses and simulations should be performed before real processing. For this purpose, traditionally, finite element simulations are usually used for warpage and stress prediction in IC packaging. Meanwhile, since the final warpage could be influenced by any processing parameters, it is essential to establish a process emulator as a tool to evaluate the impact of essential processing decision on the final performance for process optimization.
Finite element out of plan deformation contours of a reconstituted wafer to illustrate (a) symmetric and (b) asymmetric warping behavior
In our previous work, the deformation of wafer during entire wafer reconstitution process has been adequately simulated and essential parametric studies have been engaged to investigate the influence of key process parameters [4]. However, although that work yielded significant amounts of detail simulation data, the required high computational cost and lack of efficiency imply that 3D FEM is not adequate for early-stage design. That is, without a final design candidate, the simulation could be costly and extremely time consuming and this could be a major obstacle for conducting comprehensive parametric study, which is essential of design optimization. Certain material and structure equivalence and semi-analytical approaches should be adapted for enhancing emulation efficiency while keeping the accuracy to an acceptable level. In this work, we propose to integrate essential structural and material equivalences to reduce the model complexity and then develop simpler FE models for achieving cost-effective process emulation as an optimization tool for software DOE and even machine learning study in the future.
Here a rational design simulation flow is shown in Fig. 2. First, most related analytical models should be used to figure out the relationship between wafer warpage performance and possible design, processing, and material parameters. Next, to further strengthen the capability of the analytical model, improved semi-analytical models should be used for extensive DOE simulations. Once the designs have been converged, highly meshed numerical models such as full 3D FEM solvers are then applied for optimization. Due to the advantage on heterogeneous integration of FOWLP process, the corresponding full FE model could be very complicated in terms of mesh density (for compatible with critical dimensions) and material behavior variation in the process temperature levels. As a result, it is not adequate and costly to run full 3D FE extensively (for example, performing DOE).
A rational FOWLP warpage assessment flow
Instead, if one could seek a simplified 3D FE model, which is able to represent key objectives for the design, such a simplified FE model could be used to perform successful initial design, performing essential DOE, and even to generate data efficiently for data driven semi-analytical modeling. Practically, the most effective approach to reduce computational cost is to reduce analysis dimension and to reduce the number of elements/nodes in a reasonable manner. However, for FWLOP structures, it is challenging and less meaningful to reduce a 3D model into a 2D axisymmetric one. On the other hand, the complicated heterogeneous structure also prevents its further mesh simplification.
Nevertheless, one feasible approach is to simplify the heterogeneous structure into a homogeneous one through reasonable material equivalence to convert the heterogeneous (but in general individual isotropic materials) into a whole anisotropic material through material testing simulation with a representative volume element (RVE). Such an approach is considered common in micro mechanics related studies [9,10,11]. It is possible to adapt such a concept to develop material equivalence. By such an approach, critical dimensions to dominate mesh size are no longer considerations and the mesh density could be reduced significantly. However, different material equivalence approaches should achieve performance, and an optimal model should be sought.
Once the equivalent model is established, simplified 3D FE model could be built. Based on the simplified model, it is possible to perform extensive DOE for developing semi-analytical models and for design process emulators to investigate the influence of processing parameters to the deformation state of packaging wafer during processing.
Predicting wafer warpage quickly and effectively is the core of this investigation. To achieve this goal, two main subjects should be achieved, namely development of semi-analytical model and process emulators. As mentioned above, warpage and bifurcation prediction semi-analytical models were developed f

records.title: Cu-Cu混合键合原理
records.snippet: Cu-Cu混合键合是一种固态接合技术，用于芯片制造中的键合过程。与传统锡球倒装键合不同，Cu-Cu混合键合在高温下使铜原子在固态下发生扩散，形成牢固连接，避免金属熔化带来的“bridging”问题。其原理包括：选择含SiO₂介质和铜触点的晶圆，清洁表面，对位接合，100℃加热形成共价键，300-400℃高温下铜扩散实现铜-铜键合。该技术用于CIS、3D NAND等芯片产品。常见问题包括晶圆未平整、表面污染、对齐误差、铜界面有孔洞等。EVG、SUSS MicroTech、TEL等厂商提供相关设备。

records.title: 晶圆键合面（Wafer Bonding Surface）及缺陷防控（Defect Prevention and Control）
records.snippet:
白光干涉仪（White Light Interferometer，WLI）是行业主流非接触式三维形貌检测设备，严格遵循ISO 25178形貌检测国际规范，纵向检测分辨率可达0.1nm，可精准量化算术平均粗糙度Sa、均方根粗糙度Sq等面粗糙度核心参数，同时有效识别微划痕、局部形变、化学机械抛光（CMP）工艺引发的铜凹陷（Cu Dishing）等微观表面异常。
相较于原子力显微镜（Atomic Force Microscope，AFM）接触式检测设备，白光干涉仪（WLI）具备超大检测视场优势，可实现大面积晶圆表面快速扫描，兼顾纳米级检测精度与量产检测吞吐量，同时彻底规避接触式检测对超光滑键合表面造成的划伤风险，更适配半导体量产质控场景。

records.title: 玻璃基板为什么被推到先进封装前台
records.snippet:
翘曲在面板级更受关注。
玻璃基板常用的面板尺寸是 510 × 515 mm 或 600 × 600 mm，面积远大于 300 mm 晶圆。
报翘曲值的时候要分成弓形与扭曲两项，前者是球面状的弯曲量，后者是非球面对角线方向的最大偏离；同时必须写明测量温度、是自由状态还是支撑状态、边缘排除范围。
这几项不写清楚，不同批次、不同供应商的数据之间没法比较。
测量方式上，厚度与 TTV 用非接触光学轮廓沿扫描线取上下表面高度差；整片翘曲用面扫描拿到高度场，拟合到基准面后取极差。
records.query: 先进封装 玻璃基板 面板级封装 热翘曲全场光学投影在线测量

records.title: 最近先进封装圈最热的词，除了CoWoS、HBM，大概率就是“玻璃基板”了
records.snippet:
玻璃化温度能超过500℃，CTE也就是热膨胀系数还能调到3-9ppm/℃，跟硅芯片更匹配。
匹配就意味着热胀冷缩的时候，玻璃和芯片不会“各走各的”，封装应力更小，翘曲更少。
公开资料里提到，在510mm×515mm的大尺寸封装实验中，玻璃基板相较有机基板，翘曲量能减少50%以上。
还有一个经常被忽视但特别关键的点：表面平整度。
records.query: 先进封装 玻璃基板 面板级封装 热翘曲全场光学投影在线测量

records.title: 玻璃基板在共封装光学器件（CPO）中的应用与挑战
records.snippet:
相比之下，玻璃可以通过成分控制将其热膨胀系数精确设定在3-5 ppm/°C，使其与硅芯片的热膨胀系数完全一致。
因此，无论施加多高的温度，芯片和基板都以相同的速率膨胀，从而保持连接的完整性。
在实际的超大尺寸面板封装测试（尺寸为 510mm × 515mm）中，玻璃基板展现出卓越的尺寸稳定性，与传统的有机基板相比，翘曲度降低了 50% 以上。
records.query: 先进封装 玻璃基板 面板级封装 热翘曲全场光学投影在线测量

records.title: 玻璃基板在先进芯片封装中的应用与挑战
records.snippet:
在光刻过程中，整个基底会受到均匀的曝光，从而减少缺陷。
*   玻璃的热膨胀系数与上面的硅芯片相似，可减少热应力。
*   不会翘曲，可在单个封装中处理更高密度的芯片。
最初的原型产品可处理的芯片密度比有机基板高50%。
*   可以无缝集成光学互连，从而产生更高效的共封装光学器件。
*   这些基板通常是矩形晶圆，可增加每个晶圆的芯片数量，提高产量并降低成本。

records.full_markdown:
Title: Testing Silicon Photonics at Scale

URL Source: https://www.semi.org/en/blogs/testing-silicon-photonics-at-scale

Markdown Content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) are driving unprecedented demand for data movement. As bandwidth requirements climb and conventional electrical interconnects encounter limitations in power consumption, latency and reach, silicon photonics, near-packaged optics (NPO), and co-packaged optics (CPO) are becoming increasingly important technologies for next-generation data centers.

Much of the industry’s attention has focused on photonic device innovation. But demonstrating a high-performance photonic integrated circuit (PIC) is only part of the challenge. Turning these devices into products that can be manufactured reliably and economically at high volume requires a test infrastructure that can keep pace.

This represents a significant shift. Semiconductor manufacturing has benefited from decades of refinement in automated electrical test. Silicon photonics adds an optical dimension that brings new requirements for fiber alignment, coupling efficiency, polarization management, and optical instrumentation—while still requiring conventional electrical characterization.

As silicon photonics moves from development environments toward high-volume production, test becomes more than a quality gate. It is an integral part of the manufacturing strategy.

![Image 1](https://www.semi.org/sites/semi.org/files/styles/webp/public/inline-images/SEMI%20Blog%20Fig%201.png.webp?itok=Hp1woon7)

_An HVM-ready test solution requires a full complement of supporting hardware and software._

**Bringing precision optical alignment to production**

One of the most fundamental challenges is establishing a reliable optical connection to the device under test. Unlike electrical probing, where physical contact provides a relatively straightforward interface, optical testing depends on precisely coupling light into and out of very small structures.

That coupling must be repeatable from device to device and wafer to wafer. Even small variations in fiber position or angle can affect insertion loss and measured optical performance, potentially making it difficult to distinguish actual device variation from variation introduced by the test setup.

For this reason, high-volume testing requires automated alignment capabilities that can quickly locate the optical interface and optimize coupling. This can involve visual or image-based positioning to bring a fiber array unit close to the grating couplers, followed by area scans and gradient-search techniques to identify the optimal position via feedback loops – a technique typically referred to as “active alignment.” The process may also require optimization across six degrees of freedom—X, Y, and Z positioning plus three rotational axes—to maximize coupling efficiency and minimize channel-to-channel variation.

The problem becomes more complex as optical interfaces add channels. Alignment must not simply maximize one channel's performance; it must produce consistent coupling across multiple channels. Rotational alignment, for example, can influence how evenly an optical beam overlaps multiple grating couplers. Other angular adjustments can affect both insertion loss and center wavelength.

Polarization presents another variable. Because photonic structures can respond differently depending on the polarization state of incoming light, polarization must be characterized and controlled as part of a repeatable production methodology. Together, these requirements make alignment an active measurement and optimization process rather than a simple mechanical positioning step. The manufacturing challenge is to automate these functions without allowing alignment time to become a throughput bottleneck.

**Combining electrical and optical test without sacrificing throughput**

Alignment is only one part of the equation. A PIC may incorporate photodetectors, modulators, and other components requiring combinations of optical and electrical measurements. Typical characterization can include insertion loss, channel-to-channel uniformity, optical attenuation, photodetector responsivity, and wavelength-dependent behavior.

Performing these measurements sequentially can add substantial test time. A more scalable approach is to integrate electrical and optical capabilities so that operations can occur concurrently wherever possible. For example, electrical alignment can occur before optical alignment, while continuity and other electrical tests may run during automated optical probe alignment rather than waiting for that process to finish. This type of parallelism becomes increasingly important as device complexity and test coverage grow.

The same principle applies to optical instrumentation. Rather than treating each instrument as an isolated resource, high-volume environments benefit from integrated control of lasers, power meters, and other optical equipment, enabling parallel operation of multiple instruments or channels. Automated calibration and compensation are also important for maintaining measurement consistency as the test cell becomes more complex. Advantest’s development work in this area supports multiple optical instruments and parallel power-meter operation within a common test environment.

The broader objective is familiar from semiconductor test: maximize useful test coverage while minimizing test cost. What changes with silicon photonics is the number of physical and measurement domains that must be coordinated to achieve it.

**Collaboration will be essential to ecosystem scaling**

No single supplier controls all of the elements required for high-volume PIC test. The complete solution can span automated test equipment, wafer probing, optical positioning, fiber interfaces, optical instrumentation, device design, and manufacturing processes.

That makes ecosystem collaboration particularly important. Test equipment providers need to work with probe and positioning specialists, photonic device developers, foundries, and manufacturers so the interfaces among these technologies function as an integrated production system rather than individual laboratory instruments.

As an example, Advantest has collaborated closely with FormFactor to develop a wafer-level photonics test environment that combines electrical test instrumentation with wafer handling, optical instruments, and automated fiber alignment capabilities. The significance lies less in individual components than in the integration required to create a repeatable manufacturing workflow.

As silicon photonics, NPO and CPO move toward broader adoption, these collaborative efforts will become increasingly important. The industry must develop practical test methodologies that accommodate evolving device architectures while delivering the repeatability, throughput, and economics expected of semiconductor manufacturing.

![Image 2](https://www.semi.org/sites/semi.org/files/styles/webp/public/inline-images/SEMI%20Blog%20Fig%202.png.webp?itok=1HbnwvbS)

_Numerous photonics developments on the horizon will require broad industry effort to bring to fruition._

The transition from promising photonic technology to high-volume commercial products will depend on more than advances in the devices themselves. Test must evolve alongside them. By treating optical alignment, electrical and optical measurement, automation, and ecosystem interoperability as parts of a single manufacturing challenge, the industry can build the infrastructure needed to bring silicon photonics fully into the era of high-volume production.

**![Image 3](https://www.semi.org/sites/semi.org/files/styles/webp/public/inline-images/image_1031.png.webp?itok=ZIbb0snU)About the Author**

records.snippet: by D Weninger · 2026 · Cited by 36 — In this paper, we provide an overview and comparison of devices used for optical waveguide-to-waveguide coupling including inter-chip edge couplers, ...
records.full_markdown:
Abstract
In this paper, we provide an overview and comparison of devices used for optical waveguide-to-waveguide coupling including inter-chip edge couplers, grating couplers, free form couplers, evanescent couplers, cantilever couplers, and optical wirebonds. In addition, technology for efficient transmission of light through chips is discussed including guided mode and free form photonic vias for substrates including silicon, glass, and organics. The results are discussed in the context of potential applications including co-packaged optics switch packages, replaceable biochemical sensors, optically connected memory, optical computing, integrated quantum photonics, and integrated LiDAR systems to show possible improvements in energy efficiency, performance, and cost.
Similar content being viewed by others
Introduction
Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) have seen significant advancement over the past 40 years, highlighted by their rise to dominance in data center interconnects1 and the novel application of PICs in biochemical sensors2, light detection and ranging (LiDAR)3, photonic switching4, photonic computing5, and even chip based 3D printing6. While the high volume manufacturing of PICs has progressed significantly, evidenced by the fact that 103–105 devices can be integrated onto a single die1, their packaging, assembly, and testing has not. Common estimates hold PIC packaging, assembly, and testing responsible for 70−80% of the total cost of PIC manufacturing compared with only 20% for their electronic integrated circuit counterparts7,8,9,10 as shown in Fig. 1. Specifically, the data in Fig. 1a shows the breakdown for a state-of-the-art electronic system-on-chip (SoC), demonstrating that front-end-of-line (FEOL) and back-end-of-line (BEOL) fabrication processes in foundries dominates the spending of chip manufacturing11. Meanwhile, the data in Fig. 1b for PICs—in this case indium phosphide (InP)12—shows the situation reversed. Furthermore, the costs can be broken down by process as in Fig. 1c showing the most expensive processes for electronic fan-out wafer-level-packaging (FO-WLP)13, which is contrasted by Fig. 1d showing the percentage of total cost for packaging, assembly, and test processes in integrated photonics12. This discrepancy is not simply due to electronics die being substantially more expensive than photonics die overall—in fact, relatively simple PICs cost roughly equivalent to the most advanced electronic ICs. For example, a state-of-the-art electronic SoC fabricated on a 5 nm process node costs approximately $0.57 per mm2 14 to purchase from a fabless design firm before packaging, while a SiPh15 or InP PIC costs approximately $0.1–0.4 per mm2 16, respectively, before packaging for chip volumes in the several millions. This is reflected by the fact that when we look at an example electronic-photonic system, such a silicon photonic (SiPh) pluggable transceiver, the packaging, assembly, and testing still dominates the overall cost in comparison to the SiPh transmitter (Tx) or receiver (Rx) die and the required electronics die such as transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) or other drivers8 as shown in Fig. 1e.
In (a), data for Samsung’s fan-out panel level packaging (FO-PLP) manufacturing of the Google Tensor G2 system-on-chip (SoC)11. The data in (b) shows similar data for the manufacturing of a fiber coupled, integrated InP PIC with modulators and detectors12. The data in (c) is for FO-WLP, but nonetheless provides information on a breakdown by process for electronic packaging cost drivers13. Similarly, (d) does the same breakdown by process for the InP PIC12. Finally, (e) provides the overall cost breakdown for a ubiquitous electronic-photonic system—a SiPh transceiver8
Current techniques in semiconductor packaging and assembly
Electronic packaging and assembly strategies
Understanding the current technology landscape in electronic and photonic packaging can help provide answers to as to why photonic packaging and assembly continues to prove a significant challenge. Starting in 1947 with the first discrete wire connection17 in the first transistor18 and continuing with the development of ball and wedge bonding in the 1950s by Bell Labs19, electrical components have been connected using gold (Au), aluminum (Al), or copper (Cu) based wirebonds in a serial process. Today, electrical wirebonds (a 1D architecture using the nomenclature from ref. 20) can be made with 35-μm pitch21,22 and a time per bond of ~0.1 s23 using automated tools24,25, and remain the most ubiquitous interconnect modality for applications requiring <103 connections. In the 1960s, IBM proposed26 and introduced27 the first parallel process for electrical interconnection with the advent of the flip chip solder connection (a 2D architecture). Specifically, ball grid arrays (BGAs) using solder bumps coined controlled-collapsed-chip-connections (C4 bumps)28 enabled multiple connections from a die to a printed circuit board (PCB) in a single bonding step. Over time, in order to effectively scale the number of connections made to the chip, flip chip packaging strategies became more advanced with the number of intermediate substrates scaling up, as in Fig. 2a, and the solder bump diameters scaling down, as in Fig. 2b, c. Thus, for high volume applications requiring >103 electrical connections to be made, flip chip technologies are typically used.
In (a), the evolution from wirebonding (1D) to stacked die (3D) shows the increasing complexity of wiring within packages368. The plot in (b) shows the progression of bump technology over time (data up to 2020 is from ref. 369, with data after 2020 and future projections from refs. 30,370 which was in part derived from ref. 371), while (c) shows cross sections of the bumps used today, with both figures demonstrating current bumping pitches of <10 μm are possible370. The images in (d) show the common bonding processes used during assembly, which depends on the bumps technology used
Currently, advanced electronic packages are typically composed of an advanced node electronic die bonded to a redistribution layer (RDL) or embedded bridge (called a 2.1D architecture) which is fabricated on an organic package substrate, or a die bonded to a silicon interposer which is bonded to the organic package substrate (termed 2.3D or 2.5D architecture depending on if the interposer is thick enough to have electrical vias or not)29. Typically, the purpose of adding RDLs, bridges, or interposers is to achieve a higher level of electrical fan-out within the package—these components contain no functional devices on them, only Cu traces or vias. The fan-out itself is achieved by scaling the bump technology as one goes higher into the package stack, with Cu pillar bumps at the die-to-interposer level having pitches <20 μm compared to the C4 connections between the package substrate and the board having >100 μm pitch30. Stacking of electrical die atop one another (a fully 3D architecture), a practice common in the packaging of advanced dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips31 and complimentary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors32, is also possible. These 3D architectures target connection densities >104 connections per mm2 and bump pitches <10 μm by using through-silicon-vias (TSVs) combined with hybrid bonding33, which will be described below.
The processes used in the assembly and bonding of the above architectures can be grouped into four categories: mass reflow, thermocompression bonding (TCB), laser assisted bonding (LAB), and hybrid bonding. Cross sectional schematics showing the basic operation of each process can be found in Fig. 2d. The type of bonding process used depends on the type of bump used. For example, mass reflow, where die are assembled onto substrates using high speed, automated pick-and-place tools and then collectively heated in a reflow oven such that the C4 bumps melt and solidify, is often used in the case of C4

records.title: CPO (共封装光学) 测试
records.snippet: 共封装光学（CPO）测试至关重要，因失效成本极高。一旦光学引擎与交换机芯片封装，任何缺陷都可能影响整个组件。CPO测试分为四个阶段，每个阶段有不同技术挑战和设备需求。第一阶段为晶圆级单晶圆测试，EIC采用标准CMOS测试，PIC需新型双面电光探测技术。第二阶段为双面晶圆级测试，EIC与PIC键合后整体测试。第三阶段为晶粒级EPC测试，切割后单个光学引擎晶粒独立测试。第四阶段为最终测试，完成封装的CPO进行系统级测试，热管理是关键挑战。风险提示：本文观点仅代表个人，与雪球无关，投资需独立思考。

records.title: 微环调制器
records.snippet:
5.3 封装与集成
- 分立芯片集成：微环调制器芯片与驱动芯片（BUMP）通过铜 pillar 或微凸块 2.5D/3D 封装，适用于可插拔光模块。
- 共封装光学（CPO）：将微环调制器光引擎与交换机 ASIC、AI 处理器封装于同一基板，缩短电链路，降低功耗。
Intel 与 Ayar Labs 均公开演示过 CPO 方案。
- 晶圆级光学 I/O：直接在逻辑芯片晶圆上集成微环调制器（即 monolithic 或 wafer‑bonding），将光信号直接送至芯片边缘，代表“样品‑链‑网络”的最激进集成阶段，但工艺挑战极大。
